newsitem.title: USA: Electric deregulation on Texas legislative agenda.
newsitem.headline: Electric deregulation on Texas legislative agenda.

text.p: Texas' most powerful legislative leader plans to form a Senate committee to review electric deregulation, pushing the issue to the top of the agenda for the 1999 biennial legislative session.

"No state can afford to rush into a change of this magnitude," Lt. Gov. Bob Bullock said. "The change from traditional electric utility companies to a more open market presents complex challenges and obstacles that states and regions have never faced before."

During the 1997 legislative session, a deregulation bill stalled in the Senate over the issue of stranded costs. A second initiative, supported by Gov. George Bush, failed in the House in the waning days of the session.

The issue also is expected to be raised in the 1998 gubernatorial race. Bush, a Republican has no announced Democratic opponents, but Democratic Land Commissioner Garry Mauro, an ardent proponent of the state's natural gas industry, has indicated he may run.
"Bullock is showing tremendous leadership and setting up the battles for the governor's race," Tom Smith, executive director of Public Citizen, told the Austin American-Statesman.
Bullock, a Democrat, serves as president of the Texas Senate. He is regarded as one of the most powerful political leaders in the state, but is not running for deregulation.
